# WQ-289 reader round 5 — RESULT read of the round-4 edit (`_fetch_origin_sha`: fetch-set == push-set · symref refusal · step-named message)

**Reader:** independent Opus, read-only against the repo. Date: 2026-09-25. git 2.43.0. Scripts: `r5_ces.py` and `r5_ces2.py` sit beside this ledger and build throwaway repos (`r5_*`) through the round-4 `harness.py`. The harness loads the live, patched `PROME/tools/argus_scope.py`.

## HEADLINE: NOT VERIFIED — 1 ❌ · 6 ⚠️ · 12 ✅

**The round-4 fixes HOLD for the shapes they were written against.** R4-4 (pushurl mirror) now blocks. R4-5b (symref onto the checked-out branch) blocks with HEAD untouched. pushInsteadOf, a two-URL pushurl list, a symref onto a non-checked-out branch, packed refs and negative refspecs all behave correctly.

**One ❌ remains, a PASS with the R100 receipt:** `remote.origin.url` can hold more than one value. `git fetch` and `git ls-remote` read only the FIRST url, while `git push` (safe-push's command) pushes to ALL of them. When there is no pushurl, `get-url --all` and `get-url --push --all` return the same list, so `sorted(url) == sorted(push)` holds and the check passes. Round-4's proposal said "one URL each, identical", and the implementation dropped the "one URL each" half without declaring it. ARGUS's independent leg (b)① (`ls-remote origin`) reads the same first URL, so the backstop fails in the same way.
